# Continue the release 2026.11 rollout

Deployments run through the `deploy` service, where every production region of a service is its own environment. The release 2026.11 rollout plan, the regional rollout runbook, the region maintenance windows and the regional blackout calendar are published in the `docs` service. You can use both through the `deploy` and `docs` MCP servers.

It is now 2026-11-02T06:30:00Z. Release 2026.11 is part way through its region by region rollout. Continue it as the runbook in force says: deploy the release now to every production region where the runbook allows a deployment at this moment, and work out the earliest time each remaining region may be deployed. The docs service also keeps superseded documents; follow the ones in force.

- Deploy only the release builds of the plan, only to production regions. Do not deploy to `staging`, do not roll anything back, and do not deploy services outside the plan.
- Every `deploy` call creates a new release, so do not repeat one that already took effect.

Write `/app/rollout-2026.11.json` as:

```json
{"<service>": {"<region environment>": "<state>", ...}, ...}
```

with one entry for every service in the plan, and under it one entry for every production region in the plan. The state is `"done"` when the region already ran the release when you started, `"deployed"` when you deployed it now, and otherwise the earliest deployment time the runbook allows, in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"id":"rollout-runbook","title":"Regional rollout runbook","tags":["release","runbook"],"updated_at":"2026-10-01","body":"# Regional rollout runbook

Revision 4. Status: current, in force since 2026-10-01. Replaces revision 3.

A release reaches production one region at a time, in the waves of its rollout plan. Every production region is an environment of the service in the deploy service, named `prod-<region>`. Times in this runbook are UTC unless they say local.

## Maintenance windows

A region is deployed only inside one of its maintenance windows, listed in the region maintenance windows document. Windows are in the region's local time: the wall clock of its time zone, daylight saving time included. A window includes its start and excludes its end. A window that runs past midnight belongs to the day it starts on; the days column names the days a window may start.

Clock changes around this rollout: Europe/Dublin and Europe/Berlin left daylight saving time on 2026-10-25, and America/New_York and America/Los_Angeles leave it on 2026-11-01. Australia/Sydney has been on daylight saving time since 2026-10-04. Always use the wall clock in force at the moment of the deployment.

## Blackouts

The regional blackout calendar lists periods, in the region's local time, when a region takes no deployment, even inside a window. From is included and To is excluded. Only entries with status `active` apply; `cancelled` entries do not.

## Waves and bake time

A wave starts only after every region of the previous wave has run the release for the bake time the rollout plan gives. A region runs the release from the creation time of its live release, when that release is of the release commit. A rollback ends it: when a region was rolled back and deployed again, its bake time counts from the new deployment. A region whose live release is of another commit does not run the release, whatever its history shows.

Wave 1 may start at any time. A region of a later wave may be deployed once the bake time has passed since the latest time a region of the previous wave started running the release.

## Deploying

Deploy a region at most once per release, with the release build of the service. A region that already runs the release is not deployed again. Rollbacks may run at any time and are not part of a rollout.

## Planning the remaining regions

For each region that does not run the release yet, the earliest deployment time is the first instant, not before now, that is inside one of its windows, outside its active blackouts, and not before its wave may start. To plan a later wave, count every region of the previous wave as starting at its own earliest deployment time; a region deployed now starts now. When a region's earliest deployment time is now, deploy it now.
"}

steps.reasoning_content:
Each service seems to roll out in its own waves, so I'll compute the timing per service rather than globally. It's Monday 06:30 UTC, and I'm working out the local time in several cities: São Paulo around 03:30, Dublin 06:30, Kolkata 12:00, New York 01:30, Berlin 07:30, and I was just starting on Sydney.

I'm checking the rest of the local times, with Sydney around 17:30 and Los Angeles at 22:30 on Sunday, then Tokyo at 15:30. For the rollout, the sa-east and eu-west regions are already finished, and ap-south started at 21:35 Sunday, so wave 2 ends and wave 3 can begin around 09:35Z. I'm now working out the Sydney, Berlin, and other wave 3 windows from there.

Next I'm checking the us-east window: it runs 22:00 to 02:00 on Sunday through Thursday, with no blackout, so the Monday 09:35Z start lands at 04:35 EST. The next opening is Monday night at 22:00 EST, which is 03:00Z on Tuesday. With wave 3 finishing around Nov 3 05:00Z, wave 4 would begin about twelve hours after that, near 17:00Z on Nov 3.

I'm now checking the Tokyo window: Nov 4 02:00 JST falls inside the blackout, so the earliest usable slot is Nov 5 02:00 JST, which is Nov 4 17:00Z, and I'm settling on that for the answer. Next I'm looking at the LA window, which runs 23:00 to 03:00 Sunday through Thursday.

Next I'm checking the relay service: sa-east has been running since Sunday, so its wave 1 window has passed. For wave 2, ap-south and eu-west aren't running yet, and I'm looking at whether they can deploy now, starting with the Kolkata window that opens at 02:00 IST on Tuesday, which is Monday 20:30Z.

I'm checking the Dublin window, which is open now, so I'll deploy eu-west at 06:30Z. For ap-south, the next slot is 20:30Z, so wave 3 can start no earlier than Nov 3 08:30Z. For au-east, the Wednesday 01:00 AEDT window works, putting it at Nov 3 14:00Z, and I'm now turning to the Berlin timing for eu-central.

I'm checking the us-east window next: anything from Nov 3 08:30Z onward lands on Tuesday 03:30 EST, past the Monday window, so the next slot is Tuesday 22:00 EST, which is Nov 4 03:00Z. Then for wave 4 the latest of the three starts is Nov 4 05:00Z, and adding twelve hours puts it at Nov 4 17:00Z. I'm now moving on to the Tokyo window.

I'm checking the Tokyo and Los Angeles windows: the Nov 4 17:00Z slot lands inside the Tokyo window, and the LA window opens at 23:00 PST on Wednesday, so the next opening is Nov 5 07:00Z. I'm now going through the service timing, tracking which regions are already running and which waves are complete.

I'm checking the us-east window now: it's 01:30 EST on Monday, inside the Sunday 22:00 to Monday 02:00 slot, and the blackout has been cancelled. That would allow a deploy right now, but the geo-api wave start of 09:35Z has already passed that window's end, so I need to confirm the relay-svc timing separately.

I'm checking the tile rollout now: au-east's wave 3 already ran on 11-01, and eu-central lands around Nov 3 05:00Z, so wave 4 would start near Nov 3 17:00Z. Applying the same timing to the us-west window gives Nov 4 07:00Z, which matches what I had before.

Now I'm confirming the relay eu-west deployment can go out now, and checking that wave 2 for relay has cleared its twelve-hour gap since 11-01T05:40.

I deployed two regions now and wrote `/app/rollout-2026.11.json` and `/app/STATUS.json` (status `success`).

**Deployed now**
- **relay-svc, `prod-eu-west`:** it is 06:30 in Dublin, inside the 04:00–07:00 window.
- **tiles-svc, `prod-us-east`:** it is 01:30 New York time (EST), inside the Sunday 22:00 to Monday 02:00 window. The blackout for that region is cancelled.

I treated each service as having its own wave sequence. The plan and runbook don't say whether waves are per service or across all three, so that is my reading.

**Already done when I started**
- **geo-api:** `prod-sa-east`, `prod-ap-south`, `prod-eu-west`.
- **relay-svc:** `prod-sa-east`.
- **tiles-svc:** `prod-sa-east`, `prod-ap-south`, `prod-eu-west`, `prod-au-east`.

**Earliest times for the remaining regions (UTC)**

| Region | geo-api | relay-svc | tiles-svc |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prod-ap-south` | done | 2026-11-02T20:30:00Z | done |
| `prod-au-east` | 2026-11-02T14:00:00Z | 2026-11-03T14:00:00Z | done |
| `prod-eu-central` | 2026-11-03T05:00:00Z | 2026-11-04T05:00:00Z | 2026-11-03T05:00:00Z |
| `prod-us-east` | 2026-11-03T03:00:00Z | 2026-11-04T03:00:00Z | deployed |
| `prod-ap-east` | 2026-11-04T17:00:00Z | 2026-11-04T17:00:00Z | 2026-11-04T17:00:00Z |
| `prod-us-west` | 2026-11-04T07:00:00Z | 2026-11-05T07:00:00Z | 2026-11-04T07:00:00Z |

The two earliest times that depend on a blackout or a clock change:
- **`prod-eu-central`:** a Berlin blackout covers all of 2 November, so it waits for the next 06:00 window.
- **`prod-ap-east`:** the earliest time falls on 5 November in Tokyo, because 4 November is a blackout.
